access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: ecc is a library with no user interface: no CLI, no GUI and no web front end, so accessibility best practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md gives the threat model, the trust boundaries, the argument that secure design principles are applied, and how each common implementation weakness is countered. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml starts the test suite, with and without the libsecp256k1 bindings, on every push to main, and on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists. A later push to main cancels a run still in progress, and main-integrity's non_fast_forward rule, which nobody bypasses, makes the later commit a descendant of the cancelled one. btclib-org/.github#2277 records the maintainer's decision that section 10 change so that each push to main gets a run of its own. test.yml's aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check on main, and it fails while the pull request is a draft. A pull request that changes only the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists, such as CHANGELOG.md or .secrets.baseline, skips the suite, and the aggregate check still passes. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge waits for no required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by normalize_sdist.py, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release from its signed tag and runs `gh attestation verify` over the rebuilt file against the release's build-provenance attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has since made five commits, on 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses that check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, has made five commits, on 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19; pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/src/ecc/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: ecc implements every curve SEC 2, NIST and Brainpool define, not only secp256k1, and its signature and nonce functions take the curve and the hash function as parameters. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: primary purpose is to implement cryptography
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: ecc performs no network communications -- nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib -- and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
crypto_credential_agility_justification: ecc is a library with no configuration file or credential store: a private key is a caller-supplied function parameter, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_keylength_justification: Every default is secp256k1, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. Smaller curves are in the catalogue only by name, the SEC 2 v1 ones kept apart as insecure. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
crypto_pfs_justification: implements no network key-agreement protocol: dh and ecies are primitives, and whether a session built on them is forward-secret is the calling protocol's choice
crypto_published_justification: The Python arithmetic implements published algorithms (SEC 1, RFC 6979, BIP340, BIP327, draft BIP445, draft BIP458, draft BIP459, draft BIP374, BIP324, and the DLC specification's ECDSA adaptor and oracle signatures) and is validated against the specifications' own vectors. The opt-in ecc.ssa_adaptor follows the proposal in BlockstreamResearch/secp256k1-zkp#299, which no published specification includes, and nothing else in the library calls it. On secp256k1, with the optional bindings installed, a call delegates to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1 wherever its guard admits it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
crypto_random_justification: Private keys, MuSig2, FROST and DLEQ nonces, BIP340 auxiliary randomness, ECIES ephemeral keys and blinding factors come from Python's secrets module. ECDSA nonces are deterministic (RFC 6979), and nothing under src/ uses the random module. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
crypto_tls12_justification: ecc performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
crypto_used_network_justification: ecc does not use the network: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: ecc performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Every default is secp256k1 with SHA-256, and no SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/. The SEC 2 v1 curves that SEC 2 v2 withdrew are kept apart as insecure. ECIES checks its MAC with hmac.compare_digest before calling the caller's cipher. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which fails on a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses the Sign-off check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/ecc/ https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: ecc is elliptic curve arithmetic, and the signature, key-agreement and commitment schemes built on it, in typed Python. It provides ECDSA, BIP340 Schnorr, MuSig2, FROST and Diffie-Hellman among others. https://btclib.org/ecc/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges together. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md describes how src/ecc/ layers, bottom-up, from the imports, and the test test_the_layers_import_only_downwards in tests/imports_test.py holds each module to the imports its table names. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md says what ecc holds, how to install it and gives a first use, and the documentation holds the API reference. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc#first-use https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/
documentation_current_justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses that check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_interface_justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/docs/source
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's First use shows an ECDSA and a BIP340 sign-and-verify, and tests/readme_test.py runs it in the suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc#first-use
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states what a user can and cannot expect: constant-time behaviour, key zeroization, and which operations delegate to libsecp256k1. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The shipped code holds no assert statement: rg '^\s*assert\b' src prints nothing and exits 1, and git grep -n -w assert -- src/ finds the word only in comments and docstrings. So the tests and the fuzz targets, which run Python without -O, have no assertion of the package's own to enable. The asserts the test suite runs are the tests' own. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tree/main/src/ecc
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies], optional-dependencies and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: Measured with curl -sIL <URL> for each URL below, on 2026-11-14. https://btclib.org/ecc/ sends Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY, and the repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/ecc/ sends Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: deny, and no Content-Security-Policy. The documentation site https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/ sends Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and neither Content-Security-Policy nor X-Frame-Options. The criterion asks all four of the download site too, and PyPI sets its own headers.
hardening_justification: The shipped code limits what a remaining defect exposes. _blinded_jac (src/ecc/curves/curve_group.py) rescales a Jacobian point by a random factor before a multiplication, so the values the multiplication forms are not a function of the scalar alone; curve.py and curve_group.py call it. The reprs of rangeproof's secret-holding tuples, _ProveParams, NonceChain and Rewound, print no secret value (src/ecc/rangeproof.py), so a defect that logs one does not print the secret. ruff's bandit rules and CodeQL find defects before a release, and are not counted here. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/src/ecc/curves/curve_group.py
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section argues how each principle is applied, and SECURITY.md records the design decisions where a secret meets the curve. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with an EccTypeError or EccValueError; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: The package is on PyPI, so `pip install ecc` (or `pip uninstall`) is the commonly-used convention for installing and removing it; README.md gives the exact command, with the "secp256k1" extra. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is pip's, of a wheel with no installer of its own, and pip honours the standard locations: --root, DESTDIR's counterpart, writes each file at its usual path under the given root, and --prefix, --target and the active virtual environment are honoured too. Measured on 2026-11-14 with pip install --no-deps of a wheel uv build makes from the tree. https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/#install-root
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: ecc generates no end-user-facing text and sorts no human-readable strings for a locale; its output (integers, octets, points, signatures) is technical data, not text meant for localization. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/README.md
know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Common implementation weaknesses*, which names each error class for this code and the test or check that counters it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles*, which argues how each is applied here. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/LICENSE>.
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/src/ecc/__init__.py
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses that check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/ecc/
osps_br_04_01_justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses the lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user documentation is README.md's First use section, which tests/readme_test.py runs, and the API reference at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/.
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer and the source: --owner btclib-org, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml (reusable-attest.yml for earlier releases) and --source-ref the release tag, and it compares the certificate's sourceRepositoryIdentifier with this repository's id, which a rename keeps. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml gives the reason for each runtime dependency. uv obtains them from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: The criterion's details allow a platform's terms to satisfy it: "Some version control systems, such as GitHub, may include this in the platform terms of service." GitHub's do. Section D.6 of its Terms of Service, Contributions Under Repository License, has whoever adds content to a repository with a licence notice, as LICENSE is here, agree that they have the right to license it under those terms. main also requires the lint / Sign-off check, which fails on a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses the Sign-off check. https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service#6-contributions-under-repository-license https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/ecc/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The release is pure Python. Every GitHub release attaches a CycloneDX SBOM, generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires the CI status checks REPOSITORY.md lists. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md#required-checks-on-main
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs and the Sphinx inventory python.inv.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs under fuzz/corpus and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, none of them code.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists, and its aggregate check ('test: every job passed') is a required status check on main. A pull request that changes only the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists, such as CHANGELOG.md or .secrets.baseline, is accepted with no test suite run: lint, docs and the other required checks run, the suite's jobs skip, and the aggregate check passes. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge waits for no required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on a pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* says that beyond the coverage floor, new or changed functionality must come with tests of its own, added or updated in the same pull request, and a fix with a test that fails without the fix. Every change is also held to 100% line and branch coverage (standard section 8): pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, so code no test runs fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040). Read with gh api repos/btclib-org/ecc/rulesets/24033997 --jq '{name, bypass: [.bypass_actors[] | {actor_id, bypass_mode}], reviews: (.rules[] | select(.type == "pull_request") | .parameters | {required_approving_review_count, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push})}', with admin rights, on 2026-11-14; actor 3296421 is fametrano (gh api users/fametrano --jq .id). GOVERNANCE.md has the maintainer add that bypass back only in an emergency, and records that it stands until the backlog settles. It is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 36 of the 38 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.14 23 of 25, v2026.11.12 13 of 13). Counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/ecc -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-11T05:25:01Z..2026-11-12T08:14:49Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not)] | length', which prints 13 for v2026.11.12, and the same command with 'merged:2026-11-12T08:14:50Z..2026-11-14T15:24:45Z', which prints 23 for v2026.11.14. -q length in place of the filter prints each window's total, 13 and 25. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Threat model and Trust boundaries name the actors, the caller, the adversary and the libsecp256k1 bindings, and what each can do. Its Layering paragraph says which part of the package may import which. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#trust-boundaries
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's The public surface states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request that is not a draft: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge waits for neither check, and the criterion asks that every change with a violation be blocked. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request that is not a draft, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request that is not a draft (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request that is not a draft, but is not a required check. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge does not wait for the lint check, and the criterion asks that every change with a violation be blocked. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal or a refactor. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: The release notes name each vulnerability the release fixes or asks for a fix of. v2026.10.28 to v2026.11.14 fix and name no advisory; v2026.11.11's first entry says that refusals up to v2026.11.8 printed bytes of a value refused as a signature, which may be a private key (issues #495, #503 and #511), and how to find such lines in a log. v2026.10.23 names GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, fixed in btclib-secp256k1 0.8.0.10 (the secp256k1 extra asks for 0.8.0.14 or later); v2026.10.10 names the share leak of FROST's deterministic_sign (issue #168) as its first entry, and v2026.10.8 names GHSA-2wgq-4cfh-5gqh. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/tag/v2026.11.14 https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/tag/v2026.11.11
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where, and SECURITY.md takes vulnerabilities instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/issues https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker
report_tracker_justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/issues/84 . The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue.
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: The sites the criterion names (website, repository, download) are https://btclib.org/ecc/, a static page with no login form, the GitHub repository, and PyPI. The criterion's details say "Note that the use of GitHub meets this criterion". PyPI hashes passwords with Argon2: Warehouse's warehouse/accounts/services.py builds CryptContext(schemes=["argon2", "bcrypt_sha256", "bcrypt", "django_bcrypt", "unix_disabled"], deprecated=["auto"]), so argon2 hashes a password and the older schemes are deprecated. https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/blob/748d62889f7a3f77fc8282682ca77b8cbcf9abdb/warehouse/accounts/services.py#L93-L101
small_tasks_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets the label "good first issue" aside for a first contribution, but gh issue list -R btclib-org/ecc --label "good first issue" --state open lists no open issue on 2026-11-14, so no small task is identified now. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) starts on a schedule, on every pull request that is not a draft and on every push to main, and a later push to main cancels a run still in progress. ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules. Both are FLOSS static-analysis tools that look for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No static-analysis finding is open: CodeQL has no open alert, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: lint.yml and codeql.yml start on every push to main and every pull request that is not a draft, and a later push to main cancels a run still in progress: https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is measured (branch = true in [tool.coverage.run]) and the 100% gate (fail_under) includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml starts the suite on every push to main, and on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists; a later push to main cancels a run still in progress, as automated_integration_testing says. Its aggregate job, test: every job passed, is a required check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, against vectors their authors publish: the BIPs', Wycheproof's, libsecp256k1-zkp's and RFC 6979's. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says that beyond the coverage floor, new or changed functionality must come with tests of its own, added or updated in the same pull request, and a fix with a test that fails without the fix. It also makes 100% line and branch coverage a gate of the required test check, which fails on any statement or branch no test reaches. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge waits for no required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states it as written policy: beyond the coverage floor, new or changed functionality must come with tests of its own, added or updated in the same pull request, and a fix with a test that fails without the fix. pyproject.toml's fail_under = 100.0 also fails the required test check on any statement or branch no test reaches. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses that check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated by test.yml on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (fail_under = 100.0 in [tool.coverage.report]) on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than the files test.yml's prose-pattern lists. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: Recent merged pull requests change src/ together with tests of their own, such as #567, #563 and #562; gh pr list -R btclib-org/ecc --state merged -L 40 --json number,files --jq '.[] | select(any(.files[]; .path | startswith("src/")) and any(.files[]; .path | startswith("tests/"))) | .number' lists them. The required check test: every job passed also fails on a statement or branch no test reaches, which shows that a line ran, not that a test checks it. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses that check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/pull/567
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, the instructions for a change proposal, says that beyond the coverage floor, new or changed functionality must come with tests of its own, added or updated in the same pull request, and a fix with a test that fails without the fix. It also documents the 100% line and branch coverage gate, which fails the required test check on new code no test runs. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge waits for no required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v2026.11.12 and v2026.11.14, 2 of 38 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 5%, below the 50% the criterion asks (v2026.11.14 2 of 25, v2026.11.12 0 of 13); 0 were approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/ecc -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-11T05:25:01Z..2026-11-12T08:14:49Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a))] | length', which prints 0 for v2026.11.12, and the same command with 'merged:2026-11-12T08:14:50Z..2026-11-14T15:24:45Z', which prints 2 for v2026.11.14. -q length in place of the filter prints each window's total, 13 and 25, and adding and .author.login != "fametrano" inside any() prints 0 for both. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are either standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped weekly by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml
version_semver_justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/tags
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: each published advisory names the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: pmazzocchi, who reported GHSA-r5pw-9wrg-m3mj and GHSA-m38m-987v-j55h, is credited as finder on both. GHSA-2wgq-4cfh-5gqh had no outside reporter: the maintainer filed it from an audit of the organization's trees. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: GHSA-m38m-987v-j55h and GHSA-r5pw-9wrg-m3mj, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, were fixed in v2026.10.2 and published on 2026-10-02. GHSA-2wgq-4cfh-5gqh was published with its fix the day it was opened. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. enforce_admins is off, so an administrator's merge bypasses those checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
